inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU_POOL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED - pool=us-west-gpu-pool. Paging oncall: @sam (oncall)

sam (oncall): acked. I'm seeing a big queue on the inference gateway and 5xx spike in the API. Pulling metrics now.

sam (oncall): queue_length: 18,400, pending_tokens/sec: 1.2M, p95 latency: 3.6s -> normal p95 ~ 120ms. 503 rate up ~27%.

jia (runtime): I can see a deployment rollout from 3h ago — model-id: redwood-v3-tokenizer. New tokenizer defaults to anchored padding which increased average sequence length. KV-cache per-session memory approx 2.7x higher. Autoscaler events show scale attempts but hitting max_replicas=60 (org quota).

omar (ml): confirming — the v3 tokenizer PR changed padding behavior to 'pad_to_multiple_of=1024' accidentally during canary; average token counts doubled for many requests. That explains KV growth. Rolling back tokenization fix now unless runtime needs to revert model.

katie (sre): paging provider shows a hard cap from cloud vendor on GPU instances for the account (soft quota 60). We're at that cap and OOMs are increasing because each replica's memory footprint doubled. Autoscaler keeps requesting more but vendor rejects with 429_quota_exceeded.

sam (oncall): impact: multiple customers seeing elevated errors and latency; support tickets incoming. We need immediate mitigation: 1) stop rollout or route traffic off v3-tokenizer, 2) throttle heavy contexts at ingress (reject or rewrite), 3) create temporary routing to v2-small model for non-SLA customers, 4) request emergency quota bump from cloud vendor.

jia (runtime): executing steps now — applying a routing override to send production chat routes to model redwood-v2-stable for traffic tagged as non-critical. Also applying a request-rewrite at the edge to clamp max_context_tokens to 2048 for public routes. Command used: `curl -XPOST https://infra-api/services/router/overrides -d '{"route":"chat-prod","model":"redwood-v2-stable"}'`

jia (runtime): also issuing KV-cache eviction on busy replicas to reclaim memory: `rictl pool us-west-gpu-pool evict-kv --older-than 15m`

lee (support): which customers should we prioritize? I have active CS threads with alpha-corp and beta-app. Both report 50-80% request failures for their long-context endpoints.

nina (cs): drafting customer comms. Proposed subject: "Intermittent inference errors and latency — temporary routing in place". Will note we're rolling back recent tokenizer change and working on capacity.

omar (ml): initiating rollback of tokenizer change in model registry to v2-tokenize-default and pinning v3-tokenizer to canary only. Requesting release engineer to create rollback release: `releasectl rollback redwood-v3-tokenizer --to-tag v2-tokenize-default`

katie (sre): vendor contacted for quota bump; support case #CLOUD-78921 opened. ETA from vendor: ~45-90m if expedited. In parallel we should drain long-lived sessions.

sam (oncall): additional mitigation — enabling flow-control at gateway to deprioritize requests with context>2048 tokens and return `503` with Retry-After for non-critical routes. Implemented via feature-flag: `edge.max_context_tokens = 2048` and `edge.context_shed_policy=deprioritize`.

jia (runtime): patched feature-flag and restarted edge, pushing a short-lived warning banner: "Requests over 2048 tokens may experience failures; consider using summarization."

sam (oncall): quick health check after changes: queue_length -> 2,300, p95 latency -> 390ms, 503 rate -> 6%. Progress but still elevated.

lee (support): posted update in alpha-corp thread: "We detected a model tokenizer change that increased average request size; we've routed traffic to a smaller model and applied temporary limits. We're monitoring & will follow up with timeline." :white_check_mark:

omar (ml): v3-tokenizer revert completed and pinned. Canary was paused. I'm starting a controlled redeploy to confirm the rollback reduces per-session KV usage.

katie (sre): note: some replicas still show high fragmentation; planning to recycle a subset of nodes to clear driver-level GPU memory fragmentation. Command: `cloudctl instance recycle --pool us-west-gpu-pool --count 6 --reason "mem-frag reclaim"` — will coordinate with runtime for safe drain.

jia (runtime): scheduling drain of 6 nodes now. We'll shift traffic away, wait for sessions to finish or be migrated, then recycle.

sam (oncall): handoff to katie for sustained operations — I'll remain in loop for customer escalations. katie, please take postmortem and follow up with vendor quota timeline.

katie (sre): taking over. Current status summary: root cause = tokenizer padding change increased average context length -> KV-cache memory growth -> autoscaler hit vendor quota -> queue growth & throttling. Mitigations executed: routing override to v2, ingress clamp at 2048 tokens, KV eviction, node recycle planned, vendor case opened. Customer impact: alpha-corp & beta-app experienced 40-80% failures for long-context endpoints between 06:12-07:08 UTC, partial recovery ongoing.

nina (cs): sending comms to impacted customers now. Will post drafts here for review.

katie (sre): next steps: 1) confirm vendor quota bump or alternative capacity within 2h, 2) complete node recycle, 3) run load test on rolled-back model to validate memory profile, 4) postmortem with timeline and remediation including rollout gating for tokenizer-related changes (feature flags + canary traffic limits).

sam (oncall): adding note — suggest defaulting tokenizer padding to no-padding for prod until we add more robust canary checks for context bloat.

katie (sre): accepted. I'll own the postmortem and assign action items. React with :white_check_mark: when you see this if you're on the follow-up list.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated -> impact reduced, monitoring for further regressions.

sam (oncall): ended handoff. If anything spikes, page me and include `#inc-priority` tag.

(End of thread)
